title: FF-INT8: Efficient Forward-Forward DNN Training on Edge Devices with INT8 Precision
problem: Forward-Forward (FF) algorithm replaces backpropagation's backward pass but still requires heavy memory/compute for activation storage and gradient computation; INT8 quantization for training remains unexplored despite success in inference.
motivation: Edge devices have severe memory and energy constraints; FF reduces memory by avoiding backward-pass activation storage, but further optimization via INT8 quantization can unlock practical edge training.
method: Combines FF algorithm's layer-by-layer training with INT8 quantization to stabilize gradient computation. Proposes novel look-ahead scheme addressing FF limitations and improving accuracy. Layer-by-layer approach naturally partitions gradients for stable quantization. Evaluated on NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano (resource-constrained edge device).
key_novelty: First INT8 quantized training approach leveraging FF's layer-by-layer structure to stabilize gradient quantization, with look-ahead refinement for accuracy recovery.
contributions: 4.6% faster training via FF-INT8 on Jetson Orin Nano
Competitive accuracy vs. state-of-the-art through look-ahead scheme
limitations: Evaluation limited to Jetson Orin Nano; generalization to other edge accelerators and larger models not discussed.
primary_theme: INT8 quantized edge training via Forward-Forward
